title: Same Model, Different Speed: Why Your Inference Provider Matters — FriendliAI
talk_summary: A FriendliAI engineer argues that for the same open-weight model, the inference provider's serving stack (prefix caching, cache-aware routing, speculative decoding, reliability) determines real agent-workflow speed and cost.

takeaways.technique: Prefix/KV-cache reuse for repeated prompt prefixes
takeaways.what_they_do: Detect shared prefixes across requests and skip recomputing prefill for the cached portion, cutting time-to-first-token and GPU cycles.
takeaways.evidence_quote: like 50% to 80 to 90% of the tokens are identical across different requests
takeaways.numbers: 50-90% of input tokens identical across requests in real workloads

takeaways.what_they_do: Route each request to the replica that already holds the relevant prefix in its KV cache instead of load-balancing blindly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the router must send incoming request to the replica that already holds the relevant prefix in its cache

takeaways.technique: Benchmark your own workload, not vendor benchmarks
takeaways.what_they_do: Advise testing providers on your own prompts, token lengths, and traffic patterns rather than trusting published speed numbers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the only benchmark that really matters is your own workload

takeaways.technique: Treat reliability as part of speed for multi-call agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Optimize error rate and uptime alongside latency because one failed call invalidates an entire multi-step agent workflow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if just one call phase in the middle the entire workflow can be invalidated

takeaways.what_they_do: Offload less-used KV cache blocks to CPU RAM or NVMe and reload on demand to fit long contexts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: hot cache stays in GPU memory warm cachees in uh CPU RAM and quarter cache can be offloaded to MVME

takeaways.what_they_do: Dynamically choose model-based vs model-free speculation based on workload, since validation adds batch overhead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: speculation can improve per request latency but validation as overhead to the batch
